In July, Sierra Sharry and Lane Smith were expecting to become parents. Sharry was eight months pregnant. Then, Smith fell and hit his head. He was taken to the OU Medical Center in Oklahoma City. He never recovered. Sharry wrote on Facebook: "July 13th, 2014 was the worst day of my life. I lost my best friend. The father of my unborn child." Their son Taos was born a few weeks later. When it was time for his 6-month pictures, Sharry had a special request. Maybe the photographer could make their family complete, just for one picture.

Now, you have likely taken a side in the debate about Indiana’s religious freedom law. You might praise the many companies that criticize the law, saying it allows businesses to discriminate against gay and lesbian people under the guise of religion. Or, you might be like Indiana Governor Mike Pence, who is surprised by the criticism and argues that the law is essentially the same as a federal law and 29 other states. The issue is divisive because, well, the debate over religious freedom and gay rights is always intense, but also because the interpretations and motives behind the law can be questioned.

Some fans of Lucille Ball want a statue of her removed from a park in her hometown. They say the statue looks ugly and does not look like the famous actress. The life-size bronze statue is in Celoron, New York. People have compared it to singer Conway Twitty, the snake from the movie "Beetlejuice," and actor Steve Buscemi. Mayor Scott Schrecengost also said he does not like the statue. The statue shows Lucille Ball holding a bottle of a fake drink called Vitameeatavegamin. The statue has been a popular place for tourists since 2020. It is in the city where the comedian was born. It brings visitors who take pictures with the statue.

Muhammadu Buhari became Nigeria’s leader again, but this time he won through an election, not by force. This was one of the most closely fought elections in Nigeria’s history. It is important for five reasons. First, the opposition party won for the first time in Nigeria’s history, instead of the party that was already in power. Buhari, who is 72, beat the current president, Goodluck Jonathan, by about two million votes. Nigeria matters because it is Africa’s largest economy, its most populous country, and one of its biggest oil producers. It also sends a lot of crude oil to the United States.

People online and in the streets were celebrating as if Iran had just won the World Cup. But this event is even more important. Young people waved flags from their car sunroofs, played loud music, and chatted online using the hashtag #IranTalks. The excitement came after a new nuclear agreement with the United States and other world powers. This deal promises to end Iran's international isolation caused by years of harsh sanctions. Just before midnight on Thursday, Vali Asr street, one of Tehran's main roads, became like a street party. Car horns honed. Men danced in the middle of traffic. Some people showed U.S. dollar bills.

According to a court document from Brooklyn, a fourth man, Dilkhayot Kasimov, has been charged in a plot to help terrorists and for some of the men to join ISIS. The document was released on Monday. Kasimov was added to a updated indictment that already charged three other men: Abdurasul Hasanovich Juraboev, Akhror Saidakhmetov, and Abror Habibov. They are accused of two charges for helping a foreign terrorist group. Those three men have pleaded not guilty. It is not clear if Kasimov has been arrested.

On Saturday, North American early risers were treated to a total lunar eclipse, which was the third "blood moon" in a series of four. The moon entered Earth's shadow at 4:58 a.m. Pacific Time (7:58 a.m. Eastern Time). This total phase lasted nearly five minutes, making it the shortest total lunar eclipse of the century, according to NASA. The moon appeared burnt-orange before, during, and after the eclipse, which is why total eclipses are called "blood moons."

Istanbul, Turkey (CNN) – On Tuesday, people in Turkey were worried and confused. “What’s happening? What went wrong? Why can’t I use the subway?” asked an older woman wearing a white headscar and holding shopping bags. She was standing outside a closed entrance to one of Istanbul’s busiest subway stations. She was one of millions of people affected by the biggest power blackout in Turkey in over ten years. Dozens of cities across Turkey were without electricity for several hours. Millions of people were affected, including passengers stuck in stopped trains and subways.

During this Holy Week, let us remember what the Bible says about fair and decent pay. Isaiah 58.6 tells us: "This is the kind of fast day I'm after: to break the chains of injustice, get rid of exploitation in the workplace, free the oppressed, cancel debts." The McDonald's announcement that the company is going to raise wages for 90,000 of its employees is a significant victory for fast-food cooks and cashiers and those of us who support them. By standing up together, fast-food workers are making it less acceptable for profitable companies like McDonald's to pay wages so low that its workers are boxed into poverty.

The Golden State might soon be about the color of California's lawns. Governor Jerry Brown announced on Wednesday that he is imposing mandatory water restrictions on residents, businesses, and farms for the first time. He ordered cities and towns in the drought-ravaged state to reduce their water usage by 25%. "We're in a new era," Brown said. "The idea of your nice little green grass getting lots of water every day, that's going to be a thing of the past." The 25% cut in usage amounts to roughly 1.5 million acre-feet of water (an acre foot of water equals about 325,000 gallons) over the next nine months, state officials said.

It is almost time for people in the UK to vote. polling stations are getting ready to open. This election might change how the government works. The campaign was very short, especially compared to the US, where candidates take years to prepare. The result could give power to the Labour Party, led by Ed Miliband, instead of David Cameron’s Conservative government. Or it could lead to complicated negotiations as leaders try to make deals with smaller parties. We will know the answer when the polls close late Thursday evening, local time.

This is the time of year when more than 2 billion Christians around the world think about the death and resurrection of Jesus. Because of the tragic killing of Christian college students in Kenya on Thursday, and the ongoing danger against Christians in other countries, we are asking Christians this Holy Week to also think about the death, beheading, stoning, forced slavery, sexual abuse, human trafficking, harassment, bombing, and displacement of hundreds of thousands of Christians—and others— who are targeted by religious extremists just because of their faith.

The messages were found during a U U States Justice Department investigation into racial bias in the city's police and courts. The emails contain offensive comments about President Barack Obama, First Lady Michelle Obama, Muslims, and minorities. The Washington Post obtained the emails on Thursday after asking for them through a public records request. CNN reviewed them on Friday. Police Captain Rick Henke and Sergeant...

Two people, including a licensed greyhound trainer, have been arrested in Australia. This happened after at least 55 dead dogs were found dumped in the Queensland bush, according to Australian media reports. Two residents from Bundaberg, a 71-year-old man and a 64-year-old woman, were charged with one count of unlawful possession of a firearm, broadcaster ABC reported. The woman, who is a licensed trainer, was also charged with obstructing police. Michael Beatty, spokesman for RSPCA Queensland, told ABC that inquiries were continuing. The animal rights organization is assisting Queensland police in their investigation.

Two years ago, Mike Premeau and Kathy Danke started a small business called Memories Gourmet Pizza Co. in their town in Wisconsin. They were successful, and their frozen pizzas, which included breakfast pizzas and gluten-free options, were sold in stores across Nichols, an area west of Green Bay. They had a loyal customer base. But this week, all of that was threatened when people began confusing them with Memories Pizza of Walkerton, Indiana. The owners of that pizza place made national news after saying they would not cater a same-sex wedding. People left angry comments on Memories Gourmet Pizza’s Facebook page and called its phone number to protest.

A complete camel skeleton, believed to have been used by Ottoman soldiers during the 17th-century siege of Vienna, has been discovered under a cellar in Austria. The bones were found by archaeologists from the University of Veterinary Medicine Vienna (Vetmeduni) while working on a shopping center site in Tulln between 2006 and 2007. "The partially dug skeleton was initially thought to be a large horse or cow," archaeozoologist Alfred Galik said. "But a single look at the neck bones, the lower jaw, and the forearm bones clearly showed it was a camel."

Andrew Getty, the 47-year-old grandson of J. Paul Getty, died on Tuesday afternoon at his home in Los Angeles. His parents, Ann and Gordon Getty, released a statement confirming this. They also asked the media and the public to respect the family's privacy during this difficult time. Ed Winter, the assistant chief of the Los Angeles County coroner's office, told CNN affiliate KTLA that Getty's death appears to be due to natural causes or an accident. Some medication was found in Getty's home, but investigators do not know if he was taking it or what his medical history was, Winter said.

We may never fully understand why co-pilot Andreas Lubitz crashed Germanwings Flight 9525 into the French Alps on March 24, killing everyone on board. The latest report shows he intentionally made the plane dive faster. This is terrifying. As the investigation continues, we will learn more about how well Lubitz hid his mental illness and how much help he asked for. We need to ask: How did his depression affect his ability to fly? Should he have quit his job? Should his doctors have raised concerns? His case highlights important issues about people with mental illness and the shame they often face.

A man who did not want to give his name was identified by a tattoo on his neck that said "Gertrude." Kankakee County, Illinois Sheriff Tim Bukowski said this on Saturday about Kamron Taylor. Taylor is a 23-year man who was a convicted murderer and had escaped from jail until he was arrested overnight in Chicago. Authorities around Illinois had been looking for Taylor since early Wednesday when he jumped a correctional officer at Kankakee's Jerome Combs Detention Center, then took off with the guard's uniform and SUV. Surveillance video was the last officials saw of Taylor until just before midnight Friday, in Chicago. "They saw a guy that matched the description," Bukowski said.

Prince Harry, who is 30 years old, is finishing his military career. He will spend some time in Australia. He arrives on Monday for a four-week period with the Australian military. The Australian Defence Forces announced on Thursday that Harry will work and live with Australian Army soldiers in several units in Sydney, Darwin, and Perth. A spokesman for Harry said that he has already spent time with Australian troops several times during his 10-year military career.

The Florida Attorney General’s office announced on Thursday that two current Florida prison guards and one former guard trainee have been charged in a plot to kill a former inmate who was about to be released.

The men are Thomas Jordan Driver, 25; David Elliot Moran, 47; and Charles Thomas Newcomb, 42.

 According, according to CNN affiliate WJXT, an FBI informant who had been infiltrating a branch of the Ku Klux Klan called the Traditional American Knights of the Ku Klux Klan, met with these three men.

 According to court documents, Driver told the informant that he had had a fight with the inmate, and that he and Moran wanted the inmate dead ("six feet under").

Lausanne, Switzerland (CNN) – A intense week of negotiations concluded on Thursday in Lausanne. The P5+1, a group of world powers, reached a framework agreement with Iran regarding its nuclear program. The success of this agreement is still uncertain. The parties have until the end of June to work out the details and put the plan to paper. But the talks this week were, nevertheless, historic, particularly for the otherwise frozen U.S.-Iranian relationship. But that's not to say they were glamorous. In fact, the negotiations this week provided a modern demonstration of diplomacy at its best, but also at its most hectic.

On Monday morning, an homemade bomb exploded near a United Nations vehicle close to the city of Garowe in northeastern Somalia. The blast killed six people, including four aid workers from UNICEF, the international children's agency. Somalia's President said the attack was an attack against the future of the country. The attack comes after another incident on Sunday, when three African Union soldiers died in an ambush in the Lower Shabelle region of Somalia. The terrorist group Al-Shabaab claimed responsibility for Monday's attack, which happened around 8 a.m in the administrative capital of the autonomous Puntland region, according to the United Nations Assistance Mission in Somalia.

Prince Harry of Britain arrived in Australia on Monday. He will spend four weeks working with the Australian military. Before starting his duty, the 30-year prince visited the Australian War Memorial in Canberra, the capital city. He paid his respects at the Tomb of the Unknown Australian Soldier. A crowd of people gathered outside the memorial. Some took photos of the prince. One boy held a sign celebrating the prince's red hair, which read, "Red Heads Rule!" The Australian Defence Forces said last week that during his time in Australia, Harry will work and live alongside soldiers in the Australian Army in several regments in Sydney, Darwin, and Perth.

Australia, a close ally of the United States, has agreed to share some intelligence with Iran. Australian Foreign Minister Julie Bishop described the deal as an "informal arrangement," focused on tracking Australians who go to Iraq to fight for ISIS. However, one Australian lawmaker reportedly called the move "dancing with the devil." Over the weekend, Bishop became the first Australian government minister to visit Iran in 12 years, meeting with President Hassan Rouhani. The intelligence-sharing deal was announced in an interview released Monday that Bishop gave to the Australian Broadcasting Corporation while in Tehran.

Initial tests on the flight data recorder, which is often called the "black box," show that co-pilot Andreas Lubitz intentionally made the plane go down faster. This information comes from the French air accident investigation agency, known as the BEA. The black box was found on Thursday by recovery teams. These teams had been searching the mountainside in the French Alps for days since the Germanwings Flight 9525 crashed on March 24. The BEA said on Friday that its teams started looking at the black box's information right away.

After a 110-day chase across the Southern Ocean and to the coast of West Africa, the crew of a suspected poaching ship was rescued by conservationists who had been following them. The environmental group Sea Shepherd had been tracking the ship, named the *Thunder*, since their own ship, the *Bob Barker*, spotted it in the Southern Ocean several months ago. The *Thunder* is the subject of an Interpol "purple notice" for suspected fraud and fisheries-related crimes. The pursuit ended early Monday in the Gulf of Guinea, off the coast of West Africa, when the *Bob Barker* received a distress call from the *Thunder*.

16-year-old Jason Zobott goes to Huntley High School in suburban Chicago at 7:30 a.m. like other students. But what he doing after that is unusual. He is part of a special program at his school that mixes online learning with regular classroom teaching. One third of the 2700 students at the school are in this program. The school wants most students to be in this program by 2105. "This online work makes it easy for me to get my school work done," said Zobott, a top student who also does many activities outside of school. "I can learn by myself."

Days after a terrible attack by Al-Shabaab in Garissa, Kenya, launched airstrikes against the terrorist group in Somalia. A military source confirmed this. The source insisted that these strikes were not revenge for last week's massacre at Garissa University College, which killed nearly 150 people. "The latest attack of Al-Shabaab bases by the Kenya military is part of the ongoing operations that started in 211. It is not a retaliation to the Garissa attack. The operation has been ongoing," the military source said Monday. It is customary for Kenyan military sources not to give their names to media.

Pope Francis gave a traditional speech after Easter Mass. He reminded the world that the Vatican is its own country and that he acts as a moral leader. The Pope expressed sadness about the suffering of people in current conflicts and asked for all violence to stop. He specifically asked for the fighting to end in Iraq and Syria and for help to reach people who need it. "May the international community not stand by before the immense humanitarian tragedy unfolding in these countries and the drama of the numerous refugees," he said in his "urbi et orbi" address, Latin for "to the city (Rome) and to the world."

On Wednesday afternoon, Duke University students and teachers marched together, chanting, “We are not afraid. We stand together.” They were protesting after a rope noose was found hanging from a tree on campus. Duke officials asked anyone with information about the rope noose, which was discovered near a student center at 2 a.m., to call campus police. Photos of the noose caused anger in the community as they were shared on social media. At a forum held on the steps of Duke Chapel, close to where the noose was hung, hundreds of people gathered. “You came here for the reason that you want to say with me, ‘This is no Duke we will accept. This is no Duke we want. This is not the Duke we’re here to experience.

Muhanad Mahmoud Al Farekh, a 29 U.S. citizen who allegedly has ties with al Qaeda, did not enter a plea during his first court appearance on Thursday. He is charged with conspiring to provide material support to terrorists. Al Farekh was deported from Pakistan to the United States. According to a complaint unsealed in U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of New York in Brooklyn, he is accused of plotting to fight against American forces abroad. CNN counterterrorism analyst Philip Mudd said, "This is news for celebration."

The Saudi state news agency reported that a Saudi border guard was killed in a gunfight with militants in Yemen this week. The incident happened on Wednesday night in the Asir region of southwestern Saudi Arabia. The fighting began when militants in a mountainous area on the Yemeni side fired on Saudi border troops, prompting them to return fire. The Saudi media outlet said that besides the slain border guard, who was identified as Cpl. Salman Ali Yahya al-Maliki, 10 others suffered injuries that were not life-threatening. The incident marks Saudi Arabia's first publicly known military death since it launched airstrikes against rebels inside its southern neighbor.

I felt nervous about going to the Al Marmoum camel race in Dubai. As the only Gulf national on the CNN team, people expected me to know about camel racing, which is an old tradition in this area. Even though I tried to wear a kandora, a traditional outfit from the UAE, I still feel like an outsider because my modern way of life is different from this world. A friendly farm owner took us into the majlis, a meeting room where camel owners were gathering. The large room looked like a fancy theater. The camel owners sat on the floor, eating a'aish, a traditional Arabic dish made of fish and rice, which was placed in front of them. The conversation was loud and exciting.

Havana, Cuba (CNN) – Charlie Hill sits in a dark bar on a bright, sunny day in Havana. "Hey man," he says. His voice is rough from smoking, and he nods as if he knows you’ve been looking for him. Many people have been looking for Charlie Hill for a long time. For 43 years, Cuba has protected Hill from facing charges for killing a New Mexico police officer and hijing an airliner to Havana. Hill, now 65, decided to give CNN an interview after we spent two years trying to reach him. He wants to talk about how for the first time he is considering leaving his safe place and going back to the United States.

Misao Okawa, who was recognized by Guinness World Records as the oldest person in the world, died at the age of 117. She passed away on Wednesday morning in Osaka, Japan, according to Tadahi Uchimura, a local official. She survived three children, four grandchildren, and six great-grandchildren. Okawa was born on March 5, 1898. Her family was that runs a kimono shop in Osaka, according to Satoshi Yoshioka, who works at the nursing home where she has lived since 1997. "She was a person with mild character, and loved to eat so much. Her favorite food was sushi and udon noodles," Yoshioka said. "She had eaten a lot of cake for her birthday last March

Documents obtained by CNN show that the Missouri National Guard used military language, such as "enemy forces" and "adversaries," to describe protesters during their deployment to Ferguson, Missouri, last year. The guard was sent to support police officers, who were accused by community leaders and civil rights activists of using excessive force and making the tense situation worse. as sporadic protests occurred from August through the end of the year.

On Tuesday, gunmen attacked the Somali education ministry in Mogadishu, the capital of Somalia. The attack happened after a car bomb exploded. At least 12 people were killed and 16 others were hurt. officials said.

 The Islamist group Al-Shabaab said they were responsible for the attack. Abu Musab, a spokesman for the group, confirmed this. The attack started when two suicide bombers blew up a car at the entrance of the two-story building. The building is home to the Ministry of Education, Culture, and Higher Education. Mohamed Yusuf, a spokesman for the Somali National Security Ministry, said this. Five gunmen then went into the building and shot people inside, Yusuf said.

Gregory Margolin, now 87, has seen enough of war. He was a 16-year-old Jewish soldier in the Soviet Red Army during World War II. While he fought the Nazis, his family escaped. Margolin says he did not reveal he was Jewish, but it did not matter because people were being killed everywhere around him. This year, in Ukraine, he found himself in war again. Margolin was a sniper and became an army commander. His old uniform still has medals from his military time. his granddaughter Liora still is amazed by his war stories. She is surprised he survived.

365 days have gone by since more than 200 Nigerian schoolgirls were taken from their school dorms in Chibok, northeastern Nigeria. They still are missing. The Nigerian government and the rest of the world should feel ashamed that they let this happen. It is shameful that fan criminals can hurt young girls without being punished. It is also shameful that people quickly forget about such terrible things.

Norway is becoming the first country in the world to completely stop using FM radio. In two years, the switch will be finished. This does not mean people will lose radio; they will just listen to it digitally.

The Culture Minister, Thorhild Widvey, says that half of the people in Norway (a country of 5 million) already listen to digital radio.

In Oslo, officials say many people have already made the change. On FM radio, Norwegians can only find five stations. On the Digital Audio Broadcasting network, there are four times that number. Half the country already listens that way, said Culture Minister Thorhild Widvey.

Everyone is excited about a good comeback story, especially when it involves dinosaurs. For over 100 years, the Brontosaurus was removed from science textbooks, but now a new study says it should have its own name. The Brontosaurus is its own type of dinosaur, so it deserves its own name. O.C. Marsh first named the Brontosaurus in 1879, after he received 25 crates of bones discovered at Como Bluff, Wyoming, according to the Yale Peabody Museum of Natural History. Similar to, though not as large as the Apatosaurus discovered a couple of years prior, Marsh named the dinosaur, "Brontosaurus," or "thunder lizard."

Al Qaeda has offered a reward of 20 kilograms of gold (about $774,000) for anyone who kills or captures two prominent Shia Muslim leaders in Yemen. The group, called Al Qaeda in the Arabian Peninsula (AQAP), made the offer in an online news release and wanted poster. The two men are Houthi leader Abdelmalik Bedrudin Al-Houthi, who took the Yemen capital, and former Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh. The group called them “the two heads of evil.” AQAP is one of many groups fighting to control Yemen.

Doug Hughes, a 61-year-old postal worker from Florida, wrote about his plans and reasons on a website called thedemocracyclub.org before landing his gyrocopter on the Capitol lawn on Wednesday. He said that his flight was meant to highlight corruption in Washington, D.C., and to offer solutions to government corruption. He also said that his flight was not a secret, and that before he took off, he sent an email to info@barackobama.com. The letter was meant to convince the Capitol guards that he was not a threat, and that shooting him down would be a bigger problem than letting him deliver these letters to Congress.

The problems for Rio de Janeiro before the 2016 Olympics are getting worse. many dead fish were found in the Rodrigo de Freitas lagoon. The rowing and canoe events at the Olympics will happen in this city in just over a year. Rio de Janeiro’s legislative assembly started an investigation on Monday. They want to find out why the fish died in the lagoon and in other lakes and bays in the state. The investigation team will work with the State Environmental Institute (INEA) and the State Environment Secret.

Anthony Ray Hinton is 58 years old, but he is new to the outside world. Small things, like using a fork, going out at night, and going to bed without being watched, are all strange for him. He spent nearly 30 years on Alabama’s death row. until last week, when his murder convictions were wiped clean, and Hinton walked out of a county jail in Birmingham. “I have to pinch myself to tell myself that I'm free,” he told CNN’s Brooke Baldwin on Friday. “It’s going to take a little time, but I’ll get used to it.” Hinton had to get used to much worse. For 30 years, he spent most of his time locked in a 5-by-7 cell.

After the UK election debate, opinion polls showed that there was no clear winner. The debate featured seven party leaders: David Cameron (Conservative), Ed Miliband (Labour), Nick Clegg (Liberal Democrat), Nigel Farage (UK Independence Party), Natalie Bennett (Green Party), Nicola Sturgeon (Scottish National Party), and Leanne Wood (Plaid Cymru, the Welsh Nationalists). Facebook might soon need to add a new relationship status: "Just got served divorce papers." A New York judge ruled that sending divorce papers through Facebook is a legal way to serve a summons. A woman from Brooklyn, Ellanora Arthur Baidoo, is using this method to divorce her husband, Victor Sena Blood-Dzraku.

Baidoo’s lawyer, Andrew Spinnell, said they have been trying to divorce for several years but could not find Blood-Dzraku to give him the papers. Court documents say Baidoo can still call him, and he has told her he has no home address and no job.

It sounds like a scene from a science fiction movie. But it’s real. A person has a terrible accident, ends up in the hospital, and is brain dead but kept alive by machines. Doctors ask the family to donate organs to save up to eight people. Instead, the family is asked to give the whole body to save just one person. maybe a paralyzed person with a strong mind. Dr. Sergio Canavero, an Italian doctor, says we are close to HEAVEN (Head Anastomosis Venture). HEAVEN means joining the head to a new body.

Anthony Stokes’s story was expected to be a happy one, but it ended tragly on Tuesday. According to police, the teenager, who had received a heart transplant, committed several serious crimes before dying in a car crash. He stole a car, broke into a house, and shot at an elderly woman. He then led police on a fast chase before his car hit a pole and he died. In 2013, his family told the media that an hospital in Atlanta refused to give him a new heart because he had not followed the doctors' instructions. Mark Bell was speaking for the family at that time.

It was before sunrise at Garissa University College in Kenya. most students were still asleep. A few had gotten up early to attend Christian morning prayers. Then the attack began. Around 5:30 a.m. on Thursday (10:30 p.m. ET on Wednesday), the attackers started by shooting and setting off an explosion at the front gates. They kept shooting as they walked around the campus. The Red Cross reported that they stopped at a girls' dormitory. At one point, they broke into a room where Christians had gathered and took them hostage, according to lecturer Joel Ayora.

Freddie Gray, 25, was buried at New Shiloh Baptist Church in West Baltimore. A gospel choir sang for the large crowd that came to honor him. Gray died in police custody 15 days ago after he was arrested for having weapons. his death from a serious spinal cord injury caused many people to be angry about the Baltimore Police Department. Gray's death in custody is the most recent in a series of high-profile deaths involving African-Americans and law enforcement. many people have asked for answers about what happened to Gray and his funeral brought together civil rights leaders, politicians, and relatives of others who died in police custody

I have worked as a chef since I was 14, but I did not start fighting for food policy until much later. In 2007, a young girl my wife helped with was found looking through the trash for food. This made me start Food Policy Action and get involved in politics about many food issues, like hunger and factory farms. I did not work alone. One big help was "The Meatrix," a 2003 funny cartoon based on "The Matrix" made by the GRACE Communications Foundation, which showed the health and environment problems of factory farming.

Dan Swangard is a doctor, so he knows what death looks like. He has seen patients die in hospitals, connected to pain medicine and full with fear. He has watched people suffer for weeks or months while their families stood by, unable to help. But now, this is personal for him. In 22013, he was diagnosed with a rare cancer that had spread throughout his body. Surgeons removed parts of his pancreas and liver, as well as his entire spleen and gallbladder. The operation was successful but Swangard, 48, knows there's a strong chance the disease will return.

A Saudi source told CNN that Saudi special forces helped Yemeni fighters fight against Houthi rebels and their allies in Aden. The Saudi soldiers were on the ground but did not fight directly. Instead, they helped plan and guide the battle against the Houths and fighters who supported former Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh. The source said the Saudis also helped aird drops of weapons and communication equipment. Meanwhile, the source said that Houthi rebels left the presidential palace and other important areas of the southern port city of Aden after strong Saudi air attacks. This move was a change from the day before, when the Houthi forces had taken the presidential palace.

A woman from Detroit, Mitchelle Angela Blair, was charged in court this week for murder and torture. This happened after police found the bodies of two of her children in a freezer last month.

On Wednesday, Wayne County Prosecutor Kym Worthy officially charged Blair for killing her 13-year-old daughter, Stoni Ann Blair, and her 9-year-old son, Stephen Gage Berry.

According to Detroit Police Chief James Craig, a court worker who was ordered to evict the family found the bodies wrapped in plastic inside the freezer on March 24.

 A medical examiner has determined that Stoni died from multiple blunt trauma injuries and Stephen from multiple blunt trauma and thermal injuries.

Wladimir Klitschko, the world heavyweight boxing champion, has a important title fight coming up. But he is still thinking about the fight for democracy in Ukraine. Chile will soon recognize same-sex civil unions. President Michelle Bachelet signed a new law on Monday, making Chile one of several South American countries to allow these unions. The law takes effect in six months and gives legal recognition to cohabiting relationships between two people of the same sex, as well as between a man and a woman. According to a study published on Friday, China’s internet censors have found their "Great Firewall" is no longer enough. The firewall has been used for a long time to stop Chinese people from reading Western news websites or other content the government dislikes. Now, China has created a new cyber tool called the "Great Cannon." This tool has been used to attack servers outside of China, including servers in the United States. The study's authors say the "Great Cannon" works out in the open. They believe that attacking servers in other countries so openly will likely anger other countries, and that Beijing may have expected this to happen.

The investigation into the crash of Germanwings Flight 9525 has not found any evidence showing why the co-pilot, Andreas Lubitz, did it. However, a spokesman for the prosecutor’s office in Dusseldorf, Germany, said on Monday that Lubitz had shown signs of suicidal behavior at some point before he started his career as a pilot.

 Investigators have not found any writings or conversations where Lubitz explained his reasons or admitted to any plans, said prosecutor’s spokesman Christoph Kumpa. West Ham manager Sam Allardyce says defender Winston Reid will be ready to play in Saturday’s game against Leicester City. However, Enner Valencia will not be available. Reid has not played since he hurt his hamstring in a 1-0 loss to Chelsea on March 4. The New Zealand player returned to full practice during the break for international matches. Valencia missed West Ham’s last two games against Arsenal and Sunderland because of a strange toe injury he suffered at home in mid-March. Allardyce says Valencia is still not fit for match play. West Ham centre back Winston Reid (right) tussles with Tottenham's Mousa Dembele in February. "We've got Winston back in full training," Allardyce confirmed.

Five days before his wedding last May, Brittany Huber and John Redman were involved in a terrible car crash on a highway in Georgia. Brittany died, and John was badly hurt. Doctors said John would probably spend the rest of his life in a nursing home and would have to use a wheelchair. The 25-year-old assistant basketball coach at Dalton State College had a difficult future ahead of him. But, against all odds, John got better. On March 24, he helped his team to win a championship title.

Lucas, playing on the left, was with Liverpool captain Steven Gerrard during a charity game at Anfield on Sunday. Lucas, a midfielder for Liverpool, wants to return to his best form after recovering from an injury. The Brazilian player had 16 starts in 19 matches from late November. This period was also when the team’s results improved. A groin injury in February’s match against Everton made him miss 10 games. He was an unused substitute in the loss to Manchester United, which was their first league loss since mid-December. He played 90 minutes in Sunday’s All-Star Charity game at Anfield.

Are you tired of boring father-daughter photos? one photographer has found a fun way to make them better. Japanese photographer Yûki Aoyama has created a new photo series. The pictures show serious-looking teenage girls standing next to their fathers who are jumping in the air. In each photo, the daughter looks at the camera and smiles. while her father makes a dramatic pose. These images are from the 37-year-old photographer's latest book. The book's title roughly means "Daughter and Salary Man."

Police are looking for a man, who is between 50 and 60 years old, for robbing a bank. He took £3,000 in cash during broad daylight and ran away. The robbery happened at 12:30pm at a Lloyds Bank branch in Fairwater, Cardiff. Police said. Detectives have released CCTV images of the suspect, who is 5ft 9in to 6ft and was wearing black clothing. The Court of Arbitration for Sport has ended Morocco's ban from the next two African Cup of Nations. This was a punishment given by the Confederation of African Football (CAF). Morocco was kicked out of the 2017 and 2019 tournaments and fined $1 million. CAF also asked for another $9 million in compensation. This happened because Morocco withdrew as hosts due to fears about the Ebola epidemic. The Ivory Coast won the tournament in Equatorial Guinea. Morocco can now compete in the next two African Cup of Nations.

Tom Boyd thinks that Jason Denayer’s time on loan at Celtic has been so successful that he will be ready to compete for a spot at Manchester City next season. This would obviously be against manager Ronny Deila’s goal of keeping the young Belgian player for another year, but Boyd sees a positive side of it. According to the former Celtic captain, Denayer’s growth can be a perfect advertisement to encourage more young talents to take their next career step at Parkhead. The 19-year-old defender Jason Denayer (left) has impressed on loan at Celtic this season. He recently won his first international cap for Belgium in a Euro 2016 qualifier against Cyprus.

Andros Townsend scored a amazing goal for England, and he said that critics like Paul Merson gave him the motivation he needed to play well in Italy. This has been a difficult season for the 23-year-old, who hasn't reached the same level he did when he first started playing for the national team. England manager Roy Hodgson has still trusted the Tottenham player, and Townsend proved that trust was right by scoring an excellent goal at Juventus Stadium. Andros Townsend scored England's equal goal in their 1-1 friendly match against Italy in Turin on Tuesday night. Townsend celebrates his goal with his Tottenham teammates Ryan Mason (left) and Kyle Walker.

Chinese company Dalian Wanda Group has officially bought a 20 share of Spanish football team Atletico Madrid. The deal was signed at a special meeting on Tuesday. Wanda Madrid Investment’s lawyers approved the purchase of 726,707 shares for 45 million euros (32.8 million pounds). The deal was first announced in January, but two special meetings were needed to approve it. Wang Jianlin, who leads Wanda Group, wants to make Atletico Madrid more famous in Asia. Diego Simeone, Atletico Madrid’s manager, spoke to the press.

Antonio Conte said that his return to Turin for Italy’s 1-1 tie with England brought back “very fond memories,” even though reports said he received death threats in the days before the friendly match. Conte took over as Italy’s coach in August, replacing Cesare Prandelli, after Italy was eliminated in the group stage of last summer’s World Cup. However, his first seven months as national team manager have been very difficult. Italy needed a late goal from Eder to save a 2-2 tie against Bulgaria last Saturday, and Conte reportedly received death threats from Juventus fans after Claudio Marchisio suffered a knee injury on the eve of the Euro 216 qualifier.

Ian Murray thinks that the final month of the Scottish Championship season could change who finishes in second place. He believes Hibernian (Hibs) might overtake Rangers. Murray’s team, Dumbarton, has already played against both of his former clubs, Hibs and Rangers, this season, and they will face them again in the coming weeks. Even though Rangers’ manager Stuart McCall’s team is currently doing well— by winning against Hibs and Cowdenbeath—and Hibs’ manager Alan Stubbs’ team recently lost to Raith, Murray does not think Rangers will keep up their fast pace until the end of the season.

Simon Mignolet, the goalkeeper for Liverpool, took a photo with pilots inside an airplane cockpit as he flew back to England. He had just finished playing for Belgium in Euro 2016 qualifying matches against Cyprus and Israel. Although Mignolet was named in the team for both games, he did not get to play because Thibaut Courtois, who plays for Chelsea, was chosen instead. Mignolet has 14 international caps. He shared the photos of himself in the cockpit on his official Facebook account on Wednesday.

Chyknell Hall Estate, a large country property near Bridgnorth in Shropshire, is for sale for £6 million. The property includes 200 acres of land, a Grade II-listed manor house, and five cottages. The estate also has a swimming pool, a tennis court, stables, and its own cricket pitch. The main house, Chyknell Hall, was built in 1814 and has 11 bedrooms. It has only been sold twice since it was built. The secluded grounds offer complete privacy, which might attract famous buyers.

Two college police officers in Dallas are on administrative leave because of a video showing them harassing four students and arresting one after hitting him. The incident happened at El Centro College. Student Charles Adams recorded the video on his phone. He was smoking a cigarette when he saw the officers abuse the students last Wednesday. The officers approached the students while they were waiting for a bus outside the downtown Dallas campus.

Kilmarnock has made Gary Locke the permanent manager. He signed a three-year contract. Locke, 39, used as assistant manager last summer. He took over the team in early February when Allan Johnston left. Johnston was his former teammate at Hearts. Since Locke started, Kilmarnock has played seven games and lost only one. Locke will speak to reporters on Friday morning.

This weekend, one of the biggest events in German football is happening. The game, recently called "Der Klassiker," has lost some of its usual excitement. Borussia Dortmund and Bayern Munich have won the last five Bundesliga titles. Bayern is expected to keep winning this season. However, these two teams are now far apart in the standings: 31 points and nine places apart. This does not mean the game is less important than usual when these two teams play. Jurgen Klopp (center) celebrates with his Borussia Dortmund players after their win against Hannover.

14-year schoolgirl Deva Joseph was left stranded at London Stansted airport when easyJet refused to let her board her flight to Spain. because she had two pieces of hand luggage. Deva was left in tears. The teenager offered to pay for the second item to be put in the hold but was told only credit cards would be accepted - even though she is too young to have one.

Gordon Robson, 26, killed John Potts, 45, with one punch. Robson was drunk after his grandfather’s funeral. He hit Potts in the back of the head. The hit was so hard that it made a loud cracking sound. Potts fell down and died. Robson had been violent before. He was sent to prison for three and half a year. The attack happened outside a sports bar in Washington, Tyne and Wear, last November.

Scoring a goal against your old team and scoring a perfect set-piece are two of the best feelings in football. For Notts County star Ellen White, Thursday night was special because she did both against Arsenal in the Women's Super League. In the 26th minute, Notts County had a free kick near the box. Laura Bassett and Alex Greenwood seemed to mess up the play, with Bassett almost running into Greenwood. The confusion happened as Bassett and Greenwood almost collided. White spun near the box and kicked the ball into the corner against her former club.

High school girls in China are practicing military-style knife drills. They shout commands like "kill, stab, slash, and jab" while performing eight specific movements. The training is led by Inspector Tan, a former special forces soldier. The 68 students, who are between 16 and 18 years old, attend Huizhou Integrated High School. The school uses fake daggers for safety.

We spend about one-third of our lives sleeping, but many people ignore what their bodies and minds need during this time to feel rested each day. The Sleep Health Foundation released a study that shows 30% of Australians say they don’t get enough sleep every day. Professor David Hillman, who chairs the Sleep Health Foundation, says these lost hours of sleep must be made up for to stay functional throughout the week. A study shows that 30% of Australians complain about not getting enough sleep every day. The average adult needs about eight hours of sleep each night, with a range of seven to nine hours.

A video shows a fight between neighbors in Perth, Australia. that ended with a bloody attack using a crowbar. The video, posted on Facebook today, shows an angry woman shouting racist insults at a group of men who appear to be of African descent over her fence. The woman is then seen in her neighbor's front yard holding a metal crowbar, yelling at the men and swinging the tool at them. The men then pick up their own weapons and a fight breaks out. The angry woman goes into her neighbor's front yard, yelling at the men and swinging a crowbar at them. "I don't deal with monkeys, go on now you f*****g monkeys."

Valencia’s 19-year-old left back, Jose Luis Gaya, is a target for Manchester City, Arsenal, and Chelsea. All three clubs hope to sign him this summer, even though he currently plays for Real Madrid. Sports journalist Pete Jenson examines the Spanish Under-21 defender. Why are English clubs interested? His release clause is £13.5 million. Considering that Luke Shaw, who is similar in age and potential, cost £27 million, it makes sense for clubs to be interested, although there are concerns about whether he would fit in the Premier League. Jose Luis Gaya (right) plays for Valencia in a La Liga match against Sevilla earlier this season.

Police in Oregon are asking the public for help to find a motorcyclist who saved two teenagers. The police say a 59-year-old man named Edward West threatened the teens with a gun in Salem, and even told them, "get ready to die." Just then, a stranger on a green motorcycle rode in and used his helmet to knock the gun out of West's hands. This allowed the teens to run away. The police want to find the motorcyclist who helped them.

Tim Sherwood, the manager of Aston Villa, has told his captain, Ron Vlaar, that he needs to prove himself again now that he is fit to play. As the team struggles, Sherwood wants Vlaar to help them finish the season strongly. He also warned that people might have forgotten how well Vlaar played for the Netherlands in the World Cup last year, even though he missed a penalty in the semi-final against Argentina. After that, there was rumors that Manchester United might want to sign him. Now, the strong Dutch defender is returning from injury to help Villa fight against being relegated when they play at Old Trafford on Saturday.

Aston Villa manager Tim Sherwood says he is not worried about the club being sold to a new owner this summer. He wants to create his own team for next season, if the club avoids being relegated. Randy Lerner, the current owner, is talking with a potential buyer. Some people think that if a new owner takes control, Sherwood might lose his job. But Sherwood is focused on keeping the team in the league. After that, he wants to use the summer break to plan for the future.

Celtic wants to loan Jason Denayer from Manchester City again next season. But City’s manager, Manuel Pellegrini, says his young academy players are not ready for the first team. So, players like Denayer might have to come back from their loans to help the team.

Southampton manager Ronald Koeman is waiting to find out exactly when Fraser Forster will be back from his knee injury. before deciding if the team needs to sign another goalkeeper in the summer. Forster had knee surgery after falling awkwardly during a 2-0 win against Burnley two weeks ago. doctors said he could be back in four to twelve months. Koeman does not want to give a exact date for the English player and thinks Kelvin Davis is a good backup. but he admits he might have to get another goalkeeper if Forster takes longer to recover.

Steve Evans, the manager of Rotherham, was angry on the sidelines because his team almost lost and was close to being relegated. They lost a narrow game to Birmingham in the Sky Bet Championship. Birmingham took the lead in the first half with goals from Robert Tesche and Clayton Donaldson. Matt Derbyshire scored one goal for Rotherham, who were in fourth place from the bottom. Rob Kiernan, playing for Birmingham, handled the ball with his hand in a clumsy way near the 60 minute mark. This happened near Derbyshire, who went down in the penalty area. The referee, Dean Whitestone, did not give a penalty kick, which made Evans very angry. Birmingham kept their lead and won the game. Robert Tesche celebrated after scoring the first goal for Birmingham

Virgil van Dijk, a defender for Celtic, is worried because he has not been called to the Netherlands national team. The team has already let in more goals in five Euro 2016 qualifying matches than they lost in during the entire World Cup qualifying campaign. Guus Hiddink, the coach, never calls or writes. The defender made it into two squads last year. But one step forward is usually followed by two steps back. When the Dutch were drawing 1-1 with Turkey the other night he was sunning himself in the Arabian Gulf and bumping into club-mates instead. Virgil van Dijk has been in fine form for Celtic but wasn't rewarded with a call-up to the Holland national team.

Celtic has complained to the SFA about ticket prices for their Scottish Cup semi-final against Inverness later this month at Hampden. The game's governing body has already come under fire from Caley Thistle fans for scheduling the match for 12.15pm on Sunday, April 18 - before the first trains from Inverness arrive in Glasgow. Now the Parkhead club have made their feeling known after ticket prices were set at £23 for the North and South stands, with the East Stand being £15 for adults and £5 for concessions. Celtic has complained to the SFA about ticket prices for their Scottish Cup semi-final at Hampden this month.

Paul Murray, the interim chairman of Rangers, said on Thursday that the previous management teams are entirely responsible for the club being removed from the stock exchange. The club will be forced to leave the Alternative Investment Market (AIM) because it could not find a new advisor to meet the rules. Murray said the new board’s plans for the future are unchanged and that planned investments will still happen.

Wayne Rooney and his England teammates were unhappy with how they started their friendly match against Italy in Turin on Tuesday night. The game was played at the Juventus Stadium, nine months after the two teams met at the World Cup. England had won their previous seven games, so people expected them to do well. But in the first half, England played poorly and deservedly lost 1-0 when Italy’s Grazano Pelle scored with a header. Rooney, England’s captain, gave instructions to his teammates during the match, which ended in a 1-1 draw. Rooney said he and his teammates were upset by England’s performance in the first half.

Dundee United’s board responded to strong criticism from two major supporters' groups, Arabtrust and the Federation of Dundee United Supporters Clubs. These groups are " shocked" that 25 percent of £6.3 million in transfer fees for players Ryan Gauld, Andrew Robertson, Stuart Armstrong, and Gary Mackay-Steven went to unnamed parties as commissions. They also questioned chairman Stephen Thompson’s claimed level of investment in the club. The Dundee United board responded to the criticism by highlighting their on-field success.

Kilmarnock will make an official announcement on Friday morning that Gary Locke is now the permanent manager. This happens exactly eight weeks after he was first asked to manage the team until the end of the season. Locke, 39, has been given a three-year contract. He is a former manager of Hearts. On Thursday, Locke thanked the players for their hard work, which helped him gain the support of the new chairman, Jim Mann. Locke took over as caret manager in February, replacing Allan Johnston.

Chinese parents are very eager to raise child prodigies, whether they are 10-year-olds entering university or four-year-olds who can dance like Michael Jackson. Now, a new basketball star is becoming famous. A video has gone viral in China, showing a young boy performing amazing basketball skills that would make many professional players look bad. The five-year-old boy is named Mai Zizhuo. According the People's Daily Online, he has been playing basketball since he was two and a half years old. The video shows the small player making many baskets, then he runs around dribbing two basketballs.

Bayern Munich will not have David Alaba for the last games of the season. because he has torn a knee lig. Alaba will be out for about seven weeks. He was playing for Austria in a 1-1 tie against Bosnia on Tuesday when he hurt. Alaba missed three months earlier this year with a different knee injury. The 22-year-old said he is very sad but he wants to play in the last game of the season. Alaba was tackled by Emir Spahic during the game.

Hull KR has signed experienced Australian player Dane Tilse to replace Michael Weyman and Ryan Bailey, who recently left the team. Tilse comes from the Canberra Raiders.

The 30 forward stands 6 feet 7 inches tall and weighs over 17 stone. He has signed a two-and-a-half-year contract with Hull KR. He will join the team as soon as he finishes the necessary paperwork, after the Raiders agreed to let him go.

Tilse has played 200 games in Australia. He will work with his former teammate from Canberra, Terry Campese, who is now the new captain of Hull KR. Campese recently signed a two-year contract extension. Tilse is a direct replacement for Weyman, who retired last month due to injury

Mark Burchill, the manager of Livingston football team, thinks that his player, Darren Cole, will still want to play in the Petrofac Cup final on Sunday. even though the match takes place only one week after the sad death of his cousin.

The player who was once a young player for Rangers is grieving over the death of Shaun Cole, who was 22. Shaun was found dead on a street in Miami last weekend and it is thought that he was hit by a car that drove away. A soldier who had served in Afghanistan, he was on vacation in Florida while on leave and had attended a music festival there before being found on a pavement with a head injury which proved fatal. Alan Smith strongly denies that Liverpool fans attacked the ambulance he was riding in to the hospital after his serious injury. This happened nine years ago, during Manchester United’s 1-0 loss to Liverpool in the FA Cup.

Smith broke his leg and dislocated his ankle in February 2006 while trying to stop a free-kick taken by John Arne Riise at Anfield.

At the time, there were rumors that Liverpool fans tried to stop Smith’s trip to the hospital by throwing bottles, beer glasses, and stones at the ambulance, and even by shaking the vehicle.

Ronny Deila, the manager of Celtic, has confirmed that Hearts captain Danny Wilson is on their list of players to sign this summer. The Scottish newspaper Sportsmail reported earlier that Celtic might offer £400,000 for Wilson, who previously played for Rangers and Liverpool. Wilson has one year left on his current contract. Hearts owner Ann Budge says the newly promoted Edinburgh club does not need to sell him. Wilson, pictured on the right, is a a summer transfer target for Celtic and could be signed for £400,000. The defender is out of contract at the end of the season but Hearts are in no rush to sell.

Ronny Deila, the manager of Celtic, says the team will avoid a tough pre-season travel schedule to protect their chances in the Champions League. He blames last summer’s money-making tour of the United States, Austria, and Germany for a 4-1 loss to Legia Warsaw in the qualifying round. Celtic has received lucrative fees for pre-season commitments and also took trips to Australia and the Far East in recent seasons. Ronny Deila and Nir Bitton walk off the pitch after losing to Legia Warsaw in Champions League qualifying. A return to America for this July has not yet been ruled out.

Franck Ribery says that rumors about Kevin de Bruyne joining Bayern Munich are not true. De Bruyne is not a replacement for Ribery or his teammate Arjen Robben. De Bruyne plays for Wolfsburg, which is second in the league. He used to play for Chelsea, but he was mostly loaned out to other teams. Now, he has scored nine goals and has 16 assists, which is more than any other player in the league. Ribery says that even though De Bruyne is playing well, he is not the right player for Pep Guardiola. because De Bruyne plays differently than Ribery and Robben.

Kelsi Langley, the girlfriend of Arizona State University football player Davon Durant, has publicly recanted her story. She claims that her mood swings caused her to lie about being assaulted.

Durant, a highly recruited linebacker who transferred from a Kansas college, was arrested on domestic violence charges after Langley accused him of hitting her in the face and grabbing her neck during an argument in his car on March 7. Following his arrest, Durant was suspended from the football team indefinitely and could be facing expulsion.

A young boy met his hero, Detroit Tigers pitcher Justin Verlander, at a Starbucks. The boy was wearing a dark blue shirt with Verlander’s name and jersey number, 35, on the back. Verlander took a selfie with the boy and posted the picture on his Instagram account.

Eden Hazard admitted that playing so many games for Chelsea might have left him too tired to play his best. He was taken off after 62 minutes in Belgium’s 1-0 win over Israel on Tuesday. Hazard played 48 games this season for his club and his country, missing only five matches for Chelsea while helping them win the Premier League title. However, Belgium had a hard time beating Israel in their European Championship qualifying group. Hazard was replaced by manager Marc Wilmots with 28 minutes left because he had trouble beating his defender, Orel Dgani.

Police in the Northern Territory found 20 grams of marijuana hidden inside a leg of lamb. The meat was discovered after an officer noticed a strange smell. The police then x-rayed the lamb, which showed the bag of drugs inside. The lamb was being sent to a company at Darwin Airport and would have been shipped to the Tiwi Islands, 100 kilometers to the north.

Former football player Clarke Carlisle has announced that he has separated from his wife, Gemma. He is currently dealing with depression after a failed suicide attempt. Carlisle, who used to play as a defender in the Premier League, said he has moved out of the house in Yorkshire that he shared with his wife of 14 years. He tried to take his own life in December, just two days after being arrested for suspected drunk driving.

Paul Merson, a former Arsenal player, had to take back his comments about Andros Townsend. After saying that Townsend’s selection for the England team was ridiculous, he admitted he was wrong. Townsend came off the bench and scored a great goal to tie the game 1-1 against Italy in Turon on Tuesday. This was a perfect response to Merson’s comment in his Sky Sports column, where he said, "If Andros Townsend can get in (the England squad) then it opens it up for anybody." Andros Townsend scores England's equaliser in their 1-1 friendly draw with Italy in Turin on Tuesday night . Townsend celebrates his strike with Tottenham Hotspur team-mates Ryan Mason (left) and Kyle Walker . In his column for skysports.

Cesc Fabregas, a midfielder for Chelsea, seems to have a problem with his performance in the second half of the season. He was one of the worst players in the game during Tuesday's 2-0 loss to Holland. The 27-year-old was happy to be playing in southwest London earlier this week, but his performance has dropped significantly from the level he was at around Christmas, when he looked like he would break the Barclays Premier League record for assists.

West Midlands Police arrested six people in Dover this morning. They are suspected of terrorism offenses related to Syria.

The arrests happened around 8am in the departure area of the port. on the south coast. Five of the people arrested are men, and one is a woman.

 Four of the men are in their 20s and from Birmingham, in the West Midlands. The other two people are a 26-year-old man and a 23-year-old woman. They have no fixed address.

 All six people are currently being questioned at a police station in the West Midlands.

People are likely to buy treats today at 12:52 pm. A study says that people in Britain spend an average of £62 a week on rewards. The shopping for rewards reaches a high at lunchtime today. Rewards can range from as little as a bar of chocolate or a glass of wine to designer clothes and shoes, according to research by website VoucherCodes.co.uk. A study reveals that people in Britain spend an average of £62 a week on rewards, with shopping for rewards reaching a high at lunchtime today. Rewards can range from a bar of chocolate to a glass of wine. And surprisingly, men spend a third more a month than women on rewards themselves.

Arsene Wenger is very respected and known for being smart. Sometimes, you agree with something he says because it sounds right. But when you look closer, you realize it doesn’t really make sense. Usually, this happens when he talks about Arsenal’s defense. He says their defense is statistically very good, which is true, especially after their recent bad games. But last week, he talked about a different issue: a rule that might change how many homegrown players can be in a Premier League team. The Football Association chairman, Greg Dyke, wants to increase the number of homegrown players in a 25-player squad from eight to twelve.

Charlie Austin said that his close friend Joey Barton ignored him on his first day at Queens Park Rangers, but later realized his mistake. The two of them became good friends. The striker had a memorable first season in the Premier League and is being considered as a possible England debut player in the future after scoring 15 goals in the competition. His close friendship with club captain Barton is well known but their first meeting is one Austin is unlikely to forget. Charlie Austin (left) and Joey Barton have become good friends despite their very early setback.

This dog is his owner’s best friend because he saved the man from a cold, muddy situation. The black dog was filmed helping his owner at the Clarence J. Brown Dam and Reservoir in Springfield, Ohio, on Saturday afternoon. The video shows firefighters pulling the man to shore after he was in water near zero degrees Celsius for almost two hours. The man apparently got stuck in waist deep mud while getting his duck hunting gear. He was lucky to have a cell phone to call 911. First responders could not get a boat to him because the river was too shallow.

Juventus coach Massimiliano Allegri says he does not expect fans to fully support him until he wins a championship. He joined Juventus last summer, a few months after being fired by AC Milan. He has done a great job, leading Juventus to a strong position in the race for the Serie A title. Allegri, who replaced Antonio Conte last summer, will try to get three more points on Saturday when they play Empoli. Juventus manager Massimiliano Allegri directs his team from the sideline, who are currently at the top of Serie A.

Nathan Redmond scored the winning goal just six minutes after he came onto the field. in a close game. Steven Whittaker passed the ball to Redmond along the right side of the field. Redmond ran faster than defender Joe Bennett and sent a low cross into the goal. Bradley Johnson scored from the back post. This goal won the match for his team at the Amex Stadium.

The residents of Celoron, New York, are very upset about a statue of Lucille Ball, a famous person from their town. They have been upset for six years. In 202009, the town opened a statue of Ball. The face on the statue looks nothing like the funny woman they know. The locals are shocked and horrified. The statue looks so bad that a Facebook page called "We Love Lucy! Get Rid of this Statue" has more than 600 people who like it. The residents of Celoron call the statue "monstrous." The statue is based on a famous scene from Ball's show "I Love Lucy," where she is selling a health drink while drunk.

South Sydney rugby league player Issac Luke, 27, is facing a homophobic accusation because he posted an offensive comment on social media. This happened after he was attacked by fans of the Canterbury Bulldogs. Luke had previously posted a heartfelt message on his official Instagram account on Saturday, trying to find a young South Sydney fan who was allegedly attacked at ANZ Stadium in Sydney. The player wanted to give the boy a jersey before the Easter long weekend as a way to make up for the incident that resulted in the boy being hospitalized after the controversial game.

People who are afraid of spiders, watch out. This story might scare you. A man in Victoria was very surprised when a large huntsman spider came out from inside his car door handle. The video, taken in Wangaratta, in northeast Victoria, shows the man walking up to his black Holden Ute. He sprays insect repellent on the door. This forces the huntsman spider to come out from under the door handle. The man says, “Get out, you bad thing,” in a calm voice. But when the hairy spider’s legs appear, he yells and steps back in fear.

Tottenham’s manager, Mauricio Pochettino, says that Harry Kane is like Gabriel Batistuta. Pochettino also says that he will be there to help Kane when things do not go well. Kane scored on his first game for England, just 79 seconds after he came on against Lithuania at Wembley last Friday night. This move made him only two goals away from 30 goals for the season. England’s boss, Roy Hodgson wants to keep expectations low for Kane. Kane has had a fast rise after he finally got into the first team at Spurs, after he had loan spells at places like Leicester and Norwich. Pochettino says that Harry Kane is like Gabriel Batistuta.

A former professional footballer, Michael McIndoe, who played for Bristol City and Wolverhampton Wanderers, is now struggling to get basic necessities, according to a court. He previously ran a £30 million investment scheme and lived like a millionaire. McIndoe convinced other football players to join the scheme by promising them a 20% return on their money. However, the scheme failed due to growing debts. McIndoe was declared bankrupt last October with over £2 million in debt. The footballer, known as "Mr. Big" in Marbella, where he partyed with attractive women, is now being pursued by creditors through the courts.

Pavel Nedved, a director at Juventus, said that Barcelona wants to sign Paul Pogba. In an interview, Nedved, who played for Juventus 324 times, said Pogba will not be leaving the club. He also said he was happy that Juventus did not play against Barcelona in the Champions League quarter-finals.

James Oliver, 44, is a convicted sex offender. He was seriously hurt in the leg after his girlfriend, Linda Currier, 53, ran over him with her car. The police say this happened in Noblesboro, Maine, on Saturday night. NBC News reports that Currier caught Oliver trying to sexually abuse a 12-year-old girl. The police say that the couple argued inside the house after Currier saw what Oliver was doing. The police say that they found Oliver in the driveway of a home.

Brendan Rodgers, the manager of Liverpool, is trying to sign a goalkeeper named Neto from Fiorentina. But he has strong competition. PSG, and some clubs in Spain, also want Neto. Neto’s agent, Stefano Castagna, said this. Neto is 25 years old. His contract ends in June. Earlier this season, Liverpool was interested in Neto. This was when their usual goalkeeper, Simon Mignolet, was not playing. A deal for Neto in January did not happen. But it seems sure that Neto will leave Fiorentina in the summer.
